gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Technical at heart, Nippo stands small letters nearly capital-sized, each stroke looking cut from wire. And Noto Sans Marchen sits beside it, its curves ending in clear daylight, giving the wire-cut lines room to breathe.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Noto Sans Mende Kikakui reads modern and clean, with daylight through every curve and lowercase standing close to the capitals. Nippo handles loud, flat-weighted display lines; the body does the quiet work.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mono: Nippo draws small, almost capital-sized letters with wire-cut strokes that never thin out anywhere, giving a technical edge. Nippo grabs attention; Noto Sans Mono keeps spaced, sturdy words from bumping.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mro: Nippo's wire-cut strokes, with a t whose crossbar and stem share one width, give headings a technical bite. Noto Sans Mro keeps its dense, open-mouthed words moving smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Crisp, wire-cut attitude, with identical bar thickness running across every Nippo line. But Noto Sans Nabataean does the reading work, its lowercase nearly cap height and its s curves generously gapped.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Nippo makes every stroke as stout as a pipe cleaner, with small letters nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Nandinagari reads approachably for pages, thanks to generous openings and short ascenders.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa, a sans-serif with a clearly open mouth on the lowercase e, takes the text. Noto Sans Newa carries the reading, while Nippo, with no hairlines and no swells, keeps headings punchy.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke body and lifts a towering x-height, very modern. Nippo's diagonals match its stems, a wire-cut counterpoint to that sans.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Contemporary and technical, Nippo is a rope-thin outline of small, near-capital letters. Noto Sans Ogham, with wide gaps in the e and bold-looking lowercase, makes paragraphs read clean and dense.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Nippo looks drawn with a single nib, small letters nearly capital-sized and cut like wire. And Noto Sans Old Hungarian lets it lead, its large open counters staying clear at tiny sizes.
